title: Elements of Financial Statements
description: Assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, gains and losses.
html:
Building blocks of financial statements

Financial statements are built from categories called financial statement elements.

You already know several of them from Accounting Fundamentals, but now we will connect them more directly to financial reporting.

Assets

Assets are present economic resources controlled by the entity as a result of past events.

Examples include Cash, Accounts Receivable, Inventory and Equipment.

Liabilities

Liabilities are present obligations of an entity to transfer economic resources as a result of past events.

Examples include Accounts Payable, Wages Payable and Debt.

Equity

Equity is the residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting liabilities.

Equity = Assets − Liabilities

Revenue and Expenses

Revenues generally increase equity through activities related to providing goods or services.

Expenses generally decrease equity through the consumption of resources or incurrence of obligations in generating revenue.

Gains and Losses

Gains and losses may arise from transactions that are not part of the entity's main revenue-producing activities.

Example

A company sells old equipment for more than its carrying amount.

The excess may be reported as a gain.

Keep the relationships straight

  • Assets represent economic resources.
  • Liabilities represent obligations.
  • Equity is the residual interest.
  • Revenue generally increases equity.
  • Expenses generally decrease equity.
  • Gains and losses can also affect equity.
